p.i: Accinctus gladio, claues in Tibridis amnem
Quum Petri nihil efficiant ad prælia claues,

main_text.p: Quo facto (inquit Bibliander) Iulius Papa Tiberino flamini resignauit omne ius, si quod habuerunt Papæ Romani à Petro, cui dixit Dominus: Et tibi dabo claues regni cœlorum. Etenim qui claues, symbolum potestatis, abiecit ac respuit, se & successores haereditate quocq; Petrina exuit ac spoliauit.
main_text.head: 163. LEO decimus.
main_text.p: Leo decimus, patria Florentinus, ex clarissimo Mediceorum genere natus, & Ioannes Medices ante Papatum dictus, diaconus olim Cardinalis S. Mariæ in Dominica, à Cardinalibus præter omnem expectationem in demortui Iulij suffectus est locum. Bonis literis à prima iuuentute diligenter institutus, doctissimisq; præceptoribus usus, Angelo præsertim Politiano, uiro utriusq; linguæ Græcæ & Latinæ callentissimo: eruditos homines deinceps supra modum semper amauit. Decimoter-tio ætatis suæ anno, ab Innocentio octauo fiebat Cardinalis, & anno tricesimo octauo pontifex Romanus. Fuit hic Leo natura ipsa quietus ac mitis, sed ab inquietis & immitibus plerunq; gubernatus:

page.notes: Underlining in the first verse and on "Ange" in the text is ink from a reader, not printed; left out. The word "ætatis" is printed as "ætati" with a colon-like mark; read as ætatis [?]. The word "quocq;" is read as printed; the abbreviation may stand for quoque [?]. The last line is printed "tus:" at the right, the end of "gubernatus" split at the line end. Small "c"-like marks in the right margin beside "mitis" and "guberna-" are not text. Show-through from the other side is not transcribed.
